bib.title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023

question: How often can language models answer all sub-questions of a 2-hop question yet fail the composed question, does this gap shrink with scale, and can prompting narrow it?
hypothesis: Scaling improves memorised fact recall faster than compositional reasoning, and prompts that make the model state and answer sub-questions explicitly (self-ask) improve over chain of thought.
contributions: Define the compositionality gap and show it stays about 40% for GPT-3 sizes
Self-ask prompting, improving on chain of thought
Self-ask + search engine, plugging search results into follow-up answers without changing the prompt

method.summary: Evaluates GPT-3 family models with few-shot prompting on 2-hop QA. Measures the compositionality gap on CC, then compares direct, chain of thought, search and self-ask (with and without a search engine) on Bamboogle, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique. No models trained.
method.task: multi-hop (2-hop) open-domain question answering, no context passages

datasets.name: Compositional Celebrities (CC)
datasets.split: 1.2k questions sampled for the self-ask runs (Fig 6); 2 examples per category removed for prompts
datasets.source: Generated from celebrity lists (thefamouspeople.com), country properties (mledoze/countries); new here
datasets.preprocessing: Random sample manually checked for answer correctness

datasets.name: Bamboogle
datasets.source: Hand-written 2-hop questions from random Wikipedia vital articles; kept only if a search engine returned an incorrect featured snippet

datasets.name: 2WikiMultiHopQA
datasets.source: Ho et al. 2020; QA pairs only, open-domain

datasets.name: Musique
datasets.size: 1252 2-hop questions (dev); training set used to develop prompts
datasets.split: dev 2-hop only for test; train for prompt development (a few dozen experiments)
datasets.source: Trivedi et al. 2022; QA pairs only, open-domain

inference.samples: inferred: one run per question; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: Few-shot always. Direct, chain of thought, self-ask: 4-shot for 2Wiki and Bamboogle (same 4 examples as Ho et al. 2020 Table 3), 6-shot for Musique; CC uses 2-shot category-specific prompts (1-shot for self-ask in Fig 6). Self-ask appends 'Are follow up questions needed here:'. Chain of thought states the answer type before the final answer.
inference.retrieval: Search engine via SerpAPI (popular internet search engine); LM generation is stopped at 'Intermediate answer:', the sub-question goes to search, and the result (featured snippet or first-result text) is inserted into the prompt as if the LM had written it.

parameters.search_postprocessing: Davinci-002 extracts the short answer from search results for Search + postproc.
parameters.least_to_most_comparison: Zhou et al. 2022, multiple forward passes

other.prompt_development: a few dozen experiments on Musique training set; dev set used once

metrics.name: Compositionality gap
metrics.definition: Fraction of compositional questions answered incorrectly out of all those whose sub-questions are both answered correctly

metrics.name: F1 / Cover-EM
metrics.definition: Cover-EM: ground truth contained in generated answer (Rosset et al. 2020)

baselines: Let's think step by step (CC only)
eval.protocol: Single run; same questions for all systems; Bamboogle judged manually by authors; no significance tests.

prompts.purpose: Self-ask prompt, 2WikiMultiHopQA (also used for Bamboogle) (first example only; three more in Table 13)
prompts.text:
Question: Who lived longer, Theodor Haecker or Harry Vaughan Watkins?
Are follow up questions needed here: Yes.
Follow up: How old was Theodor Haecker when he died?
Intermediate answer: Theodor Haecker was 65 years old when he died.
Follow up: How old was Harry Vaughan Watkins when he died?
Intermediate answer: Harry Vaughan Watkins was 69 years old when he died.
So the final answer is: Harry Vaughan Watkins.

Question: What is the currency in Venezuela?
Answer: Venezuelan bolívar soberano
Question: What is the currency in Czechia?
Answer: Czech koruna

prompts.purpose: Direct, chain of thought and self-ask prompts for Musique (first example only; six per prompt in Tables 8-10)
prompts.text: Question: When does monsoon season end in the state the area code 575 is located?

evidence.quote: Our prompt has 4 examples, the same ones presented in Table 3 of Ho et al. (2020), in the same order

results.claim: The compositionality gap stays roughly constant at about 40% across GPT-3 model sizes and training techniques.
results.setup: Compositional Celebrities (8.6k 2-hop questions), GPT-3 Ada to Davinci and InstructGPT 001/002/003, 2-shot direct prompt
results.quote: we find that the compositionality gap remains at a roughly constant 40% between different model sizes and training techniques

results.claim: Davinci-002 answers 45.4% of CC 2-hop questions correctly with direct 2-shot prompting.
results.quote: GPT-3 (davinci-002) correctly answers 45.4% of the 2-hop questions.

results.claim: On Birth Year/Literature Nobel Winner Davinci-002 gets 1.2% of 2-hop right though it answers 80% of sub-questions.
results.note: Table 6 prints 1.1% (both subquestions right) for this category; 1.2% is the text figure for all 2-hop answers in the category.
results.quote: GPT-3 answers only 1.2% of the questions correctly.

results.claim: Compositional accuracy rises from 42.6% to 81.1% as the worse sub-answer perplexity falls (confident facts compose better).
results.setup: Davinci-002, CC, questions where both sub-questions are right; maximal perplexity bin 1.000-1.002 versus 1.232-6.738 (42.6%)
results.quote: when the maximal perplexity is between 1.000 and 1.002, the model answers 81.1% of the compositional question correctly

results.claim: ChatGPT shows an estimated compositionality gap of 42.9% and GPT-4 23.0%, with a contamination caveat for GPT-4.
results.setup: CC; GPT-4 may have seen CC since it was released before GPT-4 launched
results.quote: exhibit a compositionality gap, estimated at 42.9% for ChatGPT and 23.0% for GPT-4

results.claim: Self-ask beats chain of thought on Bamboogle by 11.2 points absolute (57.6 vs 46.4).
Self-ask + search engine reaches 60.0% on Bamboogle.
results.setup: Bamboogle, davinci-002, manually judged by authors
results.table: Table 1, row Self-ask + Search, column Bamb.
Table 1, row Direct prompting, column Bamb.

results.claim: Self-ask + search gets 40.1% EM on 2WikiMultiHopQA versus 30.0% for self-ask and 29.8% for chain of thought.
results.setup: 2WikiMultiHopQA dev subset of 1.2k questions, davinci-002, exact match

results.claim: Self-ask + search gets 15.2% EM on Musique 2-hop dev versus 13.8% for self-ask.
results.setup: Musique dev, 1252 2-hop questions, davinci-002, exact match
results.table: Table 1, row Self-ask + Search, column Musique

results.claim: Search engine alone gets 0.0% on Bamboogle (by construction of the filter).
results.setup: Bamboogle, featured snippet or first-result text

results.claim: Self-ask runs more than 30% faster than least-to-most with similar or better accuracy.
results.setup: Avg generated tokens on 2Wiki; least-to-most 844. 2Wiki acc 35.5 vs 29.0; Musique 16.3 vs 16.8 (self-ask slightly lower, 663 vs 1020 tokens). Later davinci-002 deployment than Table 1.
results.note: Table 2 self-ask accuracy (35.5, 16.3) differs from Table 1 (30.0, 13.8) because of a newer davinci-002 deployment (footnote 6).

results.claim: Zero-shot 'Let's think step by step' scores 45.7% on CC with Davinci-002 and 1.1% with Davinci, versus self-ask 79.6% and 54.2%.
results.quote: it obtained 45.7%/1.1% accuracy with InstructGPT-Davinci-002/Davinci whereas self-ask obtains 79.6%/54.2% accuracy

results.claim: 40% of chain of thought final answers on Bamboogle are not short form, versus 17% for self-ask and 3% for self-ask + search.
results.quote: In Bamboogle, 40% of chain of thought’s final answers were not in short form, while that metric was 17% for self-ask and 3% for self-ask + search engine

results.claim: Across all CC categories, Davinci-002 gets 33.4% of 2-hop wrong when both sub-questions are right and 41.8% right.
results.note: Implied gap = 33.4/(41.8+33.4) = 44%, computed from the table.
results.table: Table 6, row ALL, column Both Subquestions Right / 2-hop Wrong

results.claim: Self-ask narrows and sometimes closes the compositionality gap on CC (1-shot prompt), and chain of thought performs within 1% of self-ask; stated in Fig 6 caption, no table value.
results.note: Read from figure caption; quote is truncated by line break.

limits: Only GPT-3 models up to 175B tested; larger models might behave differently (authors).
Only English 2-hop QA; other task types tried only in limited manual experiments (authors).
No temperature, decoding or max-token settings reported; one run, no significance tests.
Bamboogle accuracy is manually judged by the authors, and has only 125 questions (less statistical power).
Table 2 uses a later davinci-002 deployment than Table 1, so numbers are not comparable across tables.
Compositionality gap only measurable on CC since other datasets lack sub-questions.
CC may be in GPT-4 training data; GPT-4 and ChatGPT estimates are indicative.
Prompt format was tuned on Musique train; davinci-002 deployments have since been retired (inferred).

terms.definition: the fraction of compositional questions that the model answers incorrectly out of all the compositional questions for which the model answers the sub-questions correctly
prompts that let the model 'talk things through' before answering, such as chain of thought and scratchpad
prompt where the model explicitly states the next follow-up question before answering it, with scaffolds like 'Follow up:' and 'Intermediate answer:'

figures.why: Side-by-side of the three prompt formats.
